# Skill Gap Analysis

## Team Skill Levels

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

skills_data = {
    "Name": ["Natalie", "Kelly", "Haydn"],
    "Python": [4, 3, 3],
    "SQL": [5, 3, 4],
    "Machine Learning": [3, 2, 2],
    "Cloud Computing": [2, 2, 1],
    "Data Visualization": [4, 3, 4],
    "Statistics": [4, 3, 3],
    "Natural Language Processing": [2, 1, 1],
    "Git/GitHub": [3, 2, 2],
    "AWS": [2, 1, 1],
    "Communication": [5, 4, 4]
}

df_skills = pd.DataFrame(skills_data)
df_skills.set_index("Name", inplace=True)

df_skills
```
```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
sns.heatmap(df_skills, annot=True, linewidths=0.5, cmap="YlGnBu")
plt.title("Team Skill Levels Heatmap")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
from collections import Counter

# Example of in-demand skills based on AI / data / IT roles
top_skills = [
    "Python",
    "SQL",
    "Machine Learning",
    "Cloud Computing",
    "AWS",
    "Git/GitHub",
    "Data Visualization",
    "Statistics",
    "Natural Language Processing"
]

# Add missing skills as 0 if not already in the dataframe
for skill in top_skills:
    if skill not in df_skills.columns:
        df_skills[skill] = 0

df_skills
```

```{python}
team_avg = df_skills.mean()

gap_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Skill": team_avg.index,
    "Average Team Skill Level": team_avg.values
})

gap_df = gap_df.sort_values("Average Team Skill Level", ascending=True)

gap_df
```


```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.bar(gap_df["Skill"], gap_df["Average Team Skill Level"])
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.ylabel("Average Skill Level (1-5)")
plt.title("Average Team Skill Levels by Skill Area")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
